article.Citation: Doering-Silveira E, et al. Report on Psychoactive Drug Use Among Adolescents Using Ayahuasca Within a Religious Context. Journal of Psychoactive Drugs. 2005.
article.Title: Report on Psychoactive Drug Use Among Adolescents Using Ayahuasca Within a Religious Context

article.IsObservational: Cross-sectional comparison of 41 adolescents naturalistically consuming ayahuasca within an existing religious community (UDV) versus 43 non-using peers; participants were not randomized or assigned to an ayahuasca protocol for research purposes, they were interviewed about pre-existing ritual practice. This is a naturalistic observational/cross-sectional design, not an RCT.
article.N: Article reports two separately-described groups: 41 ayahuasca-using adolescents and 43 non-using comparison adolescents (total N=84). Used N=41, the psychedelic-exposed (ayahuasca) group, since demographic and AE-relevant fields in this schema concern the psychedelic-exposed population specifically.
article.ArmScope: Set to psychedelic_arm because demographics (age, sex, ethnicity, marital/living status) are reported separately for the ayahuasca group and the comparison group, not pooled together; all N/demographic values used here come only from the ayahuasca-exposed group.
article.Condition: The article is a naturalistic substance-use survey, not an AUD treatment study, and does not itself label a target 'condition.' Classified as Alcohol because the paper's only statistically significant finding is a reduced proportion of alcohol users among ayahuasca adolescents (last-year use 46.3% vs 74.4%, p=0.016; recent use 32.5% vs 65.1%, p=0.006), consistent with this corpus's AUD focus. This is an inferred categorization, not an explicit label in the text — flagging for human review.
article.PctBIPOC: Article states 31/41 (75.6%) of the ayahuasca group were White and 'all others classified themselves as of mixed ethnic origin.' PctBIPOC computed as 100 - 75.6 = 24.4%.
article.PctIndigenous: Not reported. The 'mixed ethnic origin' category is not specified as Indigenous, so this cannot be inferred; coded not-reported rather than assumed equal to PctBIPOC.
article.SafetyReported: This article is a cross-sectional survey of lifetime/last-year/recent psychoactive drug use patterns (Table 1, Table 2) comparing ayahuasca-using adolescents to controls. It contains no assessment of adverse events, challenging experiences, or session-related safety outcomes from ayahuasca ingestion (no CEQ, no AE checklist, no mention of physical/psychological reactions during or after ceremonies). Because the article does not assess AE/safety at all, SafetyReported = 'N', with AnyAEReported/NumDistinctAEs/WorstSeverity/NParticipantsWithAE all set to 'NA' per the gate-consistency rules.
article.AE_denominator: Per schema, this field never takes 'NA' even when SafetyReported='N'; coded '.' since no safety population was assessed.
article.PopulationNote: Sample is adolescent (ages 15-19; ayahuasca group mean age 16.49 ± 1.34 years), younger than the typical adult samples in this corpus. Reviewed age/N fields with extra care per task instructions: N=41 ayahuasca-exposed, 23 male/18 female, confirmed against the article's own percentage figures (56.1%/43.9% of 41 ≈ 23/18).
